name: Le Repaire
storyline:
Deep inside the Algator37 universe lies a mysterious place known only as The Repaire.

No one knows exactly who created it. Some say it was built by Algator37 himself. Others believe that Douza, kSushi, BenaFett, dakime doko, and Firewolf7214 discovered it by accident.

But once you enter The Repaire, there is only one rule: you have to play.

One day, the characters receive a strange invitation summoning them to the Repaire. When they arrive, the doors suddenly lock behind them. A giant screen lights up, revealing a mysterious scoreboard and a simple message:

“Welcome to The Repaire. Prove that you deserve to leave.”

The only way to escape is to compete in a series of bizarre challenges. Seven mini-games await them, each testing a different skill: speed, memory, knowledge, deception, precision, and even their ability to manipulate the others.

But there is something they don't know.

They are not alone.

As the games begin, the Twitch chat discovers the Repaire and starts interfering with the competition. Viewers can cheer for their favorite players or unleash sabotages against whoever is leading. With every round, the Repaire becomes more unpredictable.

Friendships begin to crack. Players start lying. Alliances are formed and immediately betrayed. Nobody can trust anyone anymore.

And while the final scores begin to rise, one question remains:

Who will become the champion of The Repaire... and who will be trapped inside forever?
summary:
Le Repaire is a chaotic multiplayer party game where players compete across 7 fast-paced mini-games inspired by the Algator37 universe. Everyone gathers around a shared screen while each player uses their phone as a controller.

Throughout the game, players must be quick, clever, and sometimes a little sneaky to earn as many points as possible. The challenges range from rapid-fire games like “Tape on Douza” to the “Repaire Quiz,” as well as “The Dodge,” “Alibi Bluff,” “kSushi Says,” “The Tribunal,” and “Firewolf’s Gauge.”

But the players aren't the only ones involved. The Twitch chat can also join the chaos. Viewers can fill sabotage or hype gauges and trigger effects that disrupt the player currently leading the scoreboard. These sabotages can reduce their points, blur their screen, shorten their time, or even reverse their controls.

Each game is designed to be easy to set up and quick to join. There is no registration or installation required, and players can customize the number of rounds and choose which mini-games are active before starting.
The phone interface is designed specifically for quick thumb-based gameplay, with large touch areas and controls that let players understand what to do without constantly looking at the main screen.

The main display is built for everything from a computer screen to a TV or projector, keeping the players, mini-games, results, and scoreboard clearly visible to everyone.

Le Repaire is a mix of competition, bluffing, chaos, and audience interaction a party game where even the Twitch chat can decide to make things much more chaotic.
